new_findings_today.title: Production deploys failed repeatedly over the past 3 days from build-time Postgres statement timeouts — this run directly observed a stale deploy recover mid-session, confirming 2 already-written fixes (family pages, mobile image loading) are now live
new_findings_today.detail: Git history shows a rough 3-day stretch of build instability, all tied to the same Postgres-contention-during-concurrent-prerender root cause already tracked under NEW-2026-08-03-002/NEW-2026-08-10-002: the 2026-08-11 production build ERRORED (fixed in two steps by 3ee4aa1a and b05beac7, an uncached festivals full-table read and an oversized weekend-from join); 91cdf789 ('chore: rebuild') on 2026-08-12 notes 'auli prerender hit a transient statement timeout, c97687d7 build died at 605/5464'; and today, commit f7efea40 explicitly states 'the previous deploy of 71d248e7 ERRORED at 13:06 on /hi/quiz/hill-station with a Postgres statement timeout' and retriggers another rebuild, noting the query itself measured a healthy 276ms in isolation — 'it only fails when three build workers prerender 5,464 pages concurrently and the DB saturates.' This run independently confirmed the consequence, not just the git commentary: for roughly the first 40 minutes of this session, the live site (deploy dpl_7eDCgFSnzrD53Kqe1doDCGbjb93s, sw.js CACHE_VERSION=nakshiq-v53) was running code from BEFORE at least one already-committed, already-verified-in-source fix — 71d248e7's mobile image/service-worker fix (see detail below). Partway through this session the live deploy changed (dpl_2CQMZxrUriC7JpBXKoSSrPqJsn1j, sw.js CACHE_VERSION=nakshiq-v54) and stayed stable at that version for the remainder of the run — a rebuild succeeded while this QA pass was in progress. As of run completion, BOTH the family-page fix (eb3ab783, 2026-08-11) and the mobile image/SW fix (71d248e7, 2026-08-13) are confirmed live and working (see verification below). Nothing is currently broken on production as a result of this — this finding is about deploy-pipeline reliability, not a live user-facing defect — but 3 build failures in 3 days, now including one that visibly delayed shipping a real founder-reported mobile bug fix by most of a day, is a reliability trend worth attention before it causes a longer gap.
new_findings_today.evidence: git log --format='%h %ci %s' shows the sequence: 3ee4aa1a/b05beac7 (08-11, festivals+weekend-from build fixes), 91cdf789 (08-12, rebuild after c97687d7 build died at 605/5464), 71d248e7 (08-13 13:00:46 UTC, mobile SW fix) followed 7 minutes later by f7efea40 (08-13 13:08:02 UTC) whose commit message states the 71d248e7 deploy itself errored at 13:06 UTC on a statement timeout and retriggers a rebuild. Live verification this session: curl https://www.nakshiq.com/sw.js showed CACHE_VERSION="nakshiq-v53" (matching the 08-10 findings' recorded md5 exactly) at 12:55, 13:08, and 13:18 UTC, then CACHE_VERSION="nakshiq-v54" at 13:38 and 13:41 UTC — alongside a data-dpl-id change from dpl_7eDCgFSnzrD53Kqe1doDCGbjb93s to dpl_2CQMZxrUriC7JpBXKoSSrPqJsn1j. Family-page fix verification (eb3ab783): curl https://www.nakshiq.com/en/family/kerala at 13:41 UTC shows 26 distinct /en/with-kids/<slug> links, matching a live direct-SQL count (SELECT count(*) FROM kids_friendly kf JOIN destinations d ON d.id=kf.destination_id JOIN states s ON s.id=d.state_id WHERE kf.suitable AND s.name='Kerala' → 26) exactly; rajasthan=23, sikkim=7 similarly render real content. Itinerary fix (f1a055c0, re-verified live one more time at run's end): POST /api/itinerary returns real, non-empty day content.
new_findings_today.recommendation: No emergency action needed — the immediate symptom resolved itself and both fixes are confirmed live. Worth a proactive look at the underlying Postgres/build-concurrency contention before the next release window (the a48b1674 2026-08-06 precedent already named 'three full 5,406-page prerenders running concurrently against the same Supabase instance' as a cause) — e.g. capping concurrent build workers, or moving the highest-read pages (festivals, weekend-from, and now apparently quiz pages) further onto the cached-data.ts pattern before they also start intermittently failing builds. Also worth a lightweight alert on 'build failed, no successful deploy in N hours' so a repeated failure doesn't silently sit unnoticed the way this one did until a scheduled QA pass happened to catch it mid-recovery.

new_findings_today.title: refresh-stay-picks-agent's mandated rendered-page verification step has been silently blocked for 5 consecutive nights by an egress/proxy policy — self-reported by the job, not previously surfaced in daily QA
new_findings_today.detail: CLAUDE.md's standing rule requires running scripts/verify-touched-pages.mjs against every page touched by a DB write that changes rendered output (born from the 2026-06-10 confidence_cards incident). The nightly refresh-stay-picks-agent job writes destination_stay_picks rows and is supposed to run that verification step as part of its own run. Its own ops_reports summary for last night (2026-08-12 22:23 UTC, run status ok=true, but watchdog flags it 'needs_review') states plainly: 'render_verification: BLOCKED — this session outbound network egress policy rejects HTTPS CONNECT to www.nakshiq.com at the proxy layer... This is now the 4th consecutive night this exact block is logged for this job (also on 08-09, 08-10, 08-11 runs) — scripts/verify-touched-pages.mjs has apparently never successfully executed for this scheduled job.' Today would make it the 5th night if unresolved. The job did a reasonable substitute (read the consuming component's null-handling directly and confirmed the shape of tonight's writes matches already-live rows), so there's no specific evidence of a broken page today — but the actual mandated verification step has not run even once in the last several days, leaving the 30-minute canary-probe as the only automated safety net for this specific write path.
new_findings_today.evidence: ops_reports row for job='refresh-stay-picks-agent', run_at=2026-08-12T22:23:20.811867+00, summary.render_verification field (quoted above) and summary.no_repo_files_changed=true. watchdog's most recent snapshot (2026-08-13T02:00:48 UTC) independently flags this same job status='needs_review', last_alerts_count=1. The job's own summary explicitly requests founder action: 'either allowlist www.nakshiq.com for this scheduled sessions egress policy, or move the verify-touched-pages.mjs step to a job/environment that has network access to production.'
new_findings_today.recommendation: Founder action needed, as the job itself requests: allowlist www.nakshiq.com in that scheduled session's egress policy, or relocate the verification step to an environment that already has production access. Until resolved, this is worth a line in the pending-user-action list in CLAUDE.md so it doesn't keep silently recurring unnoticed — the job flags it every night, but nothing currently surfaces that flag to a human.

new_findings_today.title: Auto-refreshed stay-pick source-citation badges have likely never rendered for any web_search-sourced pick, due to a data-shape mismatch
new_findings_today.detail: Also self-reported in refresh-stay-picks-agent's 2026-08-12 run summary: the 'sources' column for every web_search-sourced pick (all 48 written that night, and by the job's own account this matches the pre-existing shape already live in prod) is stored as a plain JSON array of URL strings, but apps/web/src/components/editors-picks.tsx's EditorSource type expects {url, title, source_type?} objects. The component's filter (pick.sources.filter(s => typeof s.url === 'string')) silently evaluates to an empty array for every string element, so the source-citation badge never renders — no crash, no error, just a UI feature that has quietly never worked for any auto-refreshed pick.

business_summary.headline: The trip-planner fix from last week is confirmed working a week later. This week's own story is about publishing reliability: the site's build process failed three times in three days from a database contention issue already on our radar, and this audit caught it live — for part of today's check, the site was running slightly stale code, missing a same-day fix for a mobile photo-loading bug. By the end of this check, a new build had gone out successfully and both that fix and an earlier family-travel-pages fix were confirmed live and working. Nothing is broken on the site right now.

traffic_lights.area: Trip itinerary planner (last week's top fix)
traffic_lights.why: Confirmed working again today, one week on — tested with 3 different trip requests, all returned real, complete plans. Also confirmed the planner is honestly refusing to recommend places that score poorly for the requested month, even when specifically asked for them, rather than papering over a bad fit.

The site's build process failed 3 times in the past 3 days from a database slowdown issue we're already tracking. This check directly caught the site briefly running older code as a result — missing a same-day mobile photo-loading fix. A new build succeeded partway through today's check, and everything is confirmed current and working as of now. Nothing user-facing was broken, but this is worth a proactive look before it happens again with worse timing.

A second version of last week's 'silent empty result' bug pattern was found and fixed by the team this week (family-by-state pages were showing 'no results' for 36 states). Confirmed live and working today — Kerala shows 26 real kid-friendly destinations, matching the database exactly.
A real bug a visitor reported (photos not loading, especially after refreshing on a phone) was root-caused and fixed this week. Confirmed live as of this check.
22/22 core pages loading correctly, 10/10 sampled destinations available, 0 broken pages found today.

Real, confirmed progress: section headings (Emergency SOS, Why Special, etc.) are now properly translated site-wide, and all 533 destinations now have Hindi text stored in the database (up from 525 last week). What's still open: the big headline title on destination pages still shows English on the Hindi version of the site — but only for the 505 destinations using our newest page design; the older 28-page design already shows this correctly, confirming it's a scoped, well-understood gap rather than a site-wide one.
All 533 destinations still have a complete emergency-contact record (minimum 3 dialable numbers, average 7.4).

One of our nightly automated jobs (which refreshes recommended places to stay) has been unable to run its own required double-check for 5 nights in a row, due to a technical access restriction it's been reporting every night. It did a reasonable fallback check instead, and nothing looks broken, but the intended safety net hasn't actually run — flagged for a fix.

Still not fixed at the root, but this week's picture is more mixed than simply 'worse': two specific slow spots from last week (weekend-trip pages for 3 cities, and part of the search index) are now fully resolved. A separate, large, one-time database traffic spike happened for about 5 minutes on Tuesday — most likely tied to one of this week's build failures, not a new ongoing problem.
The last full accessibility/performance audit is now over 3 months old (101 days). Confirmed this week's changes don't touch that area, but it keeps getting more overdue.

The database slowdown watch item is more mixed than simply worsening: 2 specific problem spots are now fully fixed; a separate one-time traffic spike inflated this week's headline error count but looks like a one-off tied to a build failure, not steady decay.
risks: The database contention that's been intermittently slowing pages down is now also causing build/publish failures — 3 in the last 3 days. It self-resolved each time, but a proactive fix is worth prioritizing before a failure isn't caught quickly.

The nightly stay-picks refresh job's safety-net verification has been silently non-functional for 5 nights. Low risk today (a reasonable fallback check found nothing wrong), but it means we're currently trusting a weaker check than intended for that nightly write.
The Hindi headline-title gap is real and still visible to Hindi-reading visitors on the majority of destination pages, even though real progress was made this week on the surrounding page content.
The accessibility/performance audit is over 3 months stale — unchanged risk, flagged every week until it's scheduled.
bottom_line: No emergency action needed today — everything checked is either working correctly or was caught, understood, and confirmed resolved during this same check.

Worth doing soon: a proactive look at the database contention causing build failures (3 in 3 days) before it causes a longer publishing gap — likely needs either fewer concurrent build workers or moving a couple more page types onto the site's caching system.
Worth doing soon: unblock the nightly stay-picks job's safety-check step (a simple network-access allowlist fix per the job's own diagnosis).
Worth scheduling: the overdue accessibility/performance audit (now over 3 months stale) and the remaining Hindi headline-title gap (scoped now to a specific page template, not site-wide).
